origin.description: Computes the lower and upper confidence limits for survival, given the survival estimate p and its standard error se, on the plain, log, log-log, logit or arcsin scale.
origin.usage: survfit_confint(p, se, logse=TRUE, conf.type, conf.int=.95, selow, ulimit=TRUE)
origin.details: When logse is FALSE, se is the standard error of the survival rather than of its log. selow is the lower-side standard error used by the modified lower limit. ulimit caps the plain and log upper limits at 1.
origin.value: A list with lower and upper.
origin.example:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(survival))
ci <- survival::survfit_confint(c(0.9, 0.5), c(0.05, 0.1), conf.type = "log")
cat(sprintf("%.6f", ci$lower), "\n")
cat(sprintf("%.6f", ci$upper), "\n")

translation.description: Computes the lower and upper confidence limits for survival, given the survival estimate p and its standard error se, on the plain, log, log-log, logit or arcsin scale.
translation.usage: survfit_confint(p, se, logse=True, conf_type=None, conf_int=0.95, selow=None, ulimit=True)
translation.details: conf_type is required. Use NumPy arrays for p and se. Results are a dict with lower and upper arrays. The normal quantile comes from the standard library NormalDist.
translation.value: A dict with lower and upper arrays.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from survival.survfit_confint import survfit_confint

ci = survfit_confint(np.array([0.9, 0.5]), np.array([0.05, 0.1]), conf_type="log")
print(" ".join(f"{v:.6f}" for v in ci["lower"]))
print(" ".join(f"{v:.6f}" for v in ci["upper"]))
